_comment: addrd config for the hivre.com DNS-experimentation lab (homelab
docs/plans/dns-experimentation-lab.md).
WEB TIER ONLY -- this instance serves NO DNS.
All authoritative DNS for hivre.com is CoreDNS's job: the hidden primary
for the apex zone, and a purpose-written probe-zone plugin for
check.hivre.com. Two reasons it is not addrd's job:
1. Response Rate Limiting. github.com/coredns/rrl is wired into the
CoreDNS build and is what gates exposing any authoritative zone of
ours to the public internet. It protects CoreDNS only. A probe zone
served by addrd would be the single directly-public authoritative
listener with no RRL in front of it -- precisely backwards.
2. Licensing. This fork is AGPL-3.0; the CoreDNS plugin repo is MIT.
Keeping the two as separate programs that share nothing but a Valkey
key space keeps that boundary clean -- no linking, no combined work.
Every zone block in internal/config is individually nil/len guarded, so
omitting DnscheckZones / ChallengesZone / DynZone / MyaddrZones disables
them outright with no code change, and the DNS listeners answer nothing.
KNOWN GAP, not solved by config alone: the /watch/{watcher} websocket --
the live 'here is what your resolver did' stream -- is registered inside
the `len(config.DnscheckZones) > 0` block in internal/config/config.go and
is fed in-process by addrd's own DNS handler pushing into a
dnscheck.SimpleWatcherHub. With zones disabled it is neither registered
nor fed. Serving the UI web-only therefore requires feeding that hub from
Valkey (what the CoreDNS probe plugin writes) instead of from a local DNS
handler. Upstream also has no /api/report?token= endpoint at all -- its
design is websocket push, not a report store -- so the plan's report-API
shape is ours to add.
What IS reusable unmodified: the SPA under website/dnscheck.tools/, and
the /dns/{name}/{type} JSON lookup handler, which is registered
independently of any zone and needs only LookupUpstream.
_comment_socket: Keep this path SHORT. It is a unix socket, so the whole path must fit in
'bind: invalid argument' -- which names neither the length nor the path --
when it doesn't. Easy to trip in Kubernetes, where a volume path plus a
generated pod/subpath name gets long fast. Traefik fronts this socket
_comment_valkey: The label-correlation store, and the seam between the two programs: the
CoreDNS probe plugin writes label -> observation, this web tier reads.
Points at the existing Valkey HA cluster. Short TTLs, disposable state,
so this pod stays stateless -- do not set DatabasePath alongside it.
_comment_lookup: Recursive resolver behind the /dns/{name}/{type} JSON lookup endpoint.
The plan calls for Unbound with `ede: yes` so Extended DNS Errors and the
AD bit are real rather than synthesised. Any validating resolver works
until that exists, but EDE readouts will be empty.
SECURITY: never let this become an open 'look up anything' proxy -- that
is a reconnaissance relay and an amplification reflector using our IP.
Restrict names to hivre.com zones or a small curated allowlist and
validate the type against a short enum before this ships publicly.
